title: Add Prometheus metrics + tracing attributes for data residency enforcement checks
author: Caleb Johnson
release_notes: Adds first-class metrics and trace attributes for residency policy evaluation/violations to support beta rollout monitoring and alerting.
description:
Context: As part of Hosted Data Residency Enforcement, we need consistent telemetry to answer (a) are we enforcing in the right place, (b) what decisions are being made, (c) who is being impacted, and (d) are violations due to customer config vs routing behavior vs control-plane issues. This PR adds Prometheus counters/histograms + standard trace attributes for residency checks. It also includes references to a Grafana dashboard JSON stub (full panels/alerts are being built in observability-pack PRs). Changes: 1) Prometheus metrics: - redwood_residency_check_total{decision, reason, request_region, pinned_region, policy_mode, org_tier, product_surface} - redwood_residency_check_duration_seconds{decision, policy_mode} - redwood_residency_policy_cache_result_total{result, policy_mode} (hit/miss/stale/error) - redwood_residency_enforcement_fail_closed_total{component} (gateway/router/storage) Notes on labels: - decision: allow|deny|error - reason: region_mismatch|policy_missing|policy_invalid|evaluator_unavailable|override_enabled|cross_region_fallback_blocked|unknown (kept low-cardinality; request_id is NOT a label) - request_region is the region resolved from the incoming endpoint / gateway region; pinned_region is the effective pinned region after policy evaluation (or "" when unset) - org_tier: free|pro|enterprise (derived from org tier at admission; not from billing pipeline) 2) Tracing attributes (OpenTelemetry): - residency.enabled (bool) - residency.decision (string: allow|deny|error) - residency.reason (string; matches metric reason) - residency.request_region (string) - residency.pinned_region (string) - residency.allowed_regions (string; comma-separated for logs/trace only; NOT emitted as metric label) - residency.policy_source (string: org|project|workspace|default) 3) Logging: - Adds structured log fields consistent with tracing attributes for the residency decision log line emitted at request admission. 4) Dashboard stub references: - Adds a minimal dashboard JSON stub and wiring hook for future panels. The stub is not intended to be imported as-is; it primarily reserves metric names/label conventions and links to the runbook. See follow-ups in observability-pack. Testing/validation: - Unit tests for metric emission on allow/deny paths. - Ensures metric label values are sanitized (unknown/empty collapsed) and reason remains bounded. - Manual validation in staging: verified metrics appear under /metrics on gateway pods and trace attributes show in Tempo for residency_violation sample. Rollout considerations: - Metrics are behind the existing residency enforcement feature flag; if flag is off, we still emit redwood_residency_check_total with decision="allow" and reason="policy_missing" ONLY when policy evaluator is invoked (current behavior is: evaluator not invoked when enforcement disabled). - No PII: request_id/prompt content not included in metrics/trace attributes. - Cardinality: request_region and pinned_region are bounded to known region identifiers; org_tier is bounded; reason is bounded.

Refs: Linear ENG-2845 (observability), ENG-2842 (gateway enforcement). Related: PR 18435 (gateway middleware), PR 18466 (audit events).
commits: metrics: introduce residency metrics registry + helpers
tracing: add standard residency trace attributes at admission
gateway: emit decision metrics for allow/deny/error paths
policy-evaluator: add cache hit/miss counters for residency lookups
dashboards: add residency dashboard stub + runbook link
tests: add unit tests for label bounding + denial path emission
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we confirm label cardinality here? In particular, allowed_regions should not be a metric label. Also, please align attribute key naming with our OTel conventions (dot-separated, lower-case). Caleb Johnson (author): Yep—allowed_regions is trace/log only (comma-separated string). Metrics only get request_region + pinned_region. I also updated keys to residency.request_region etc. per packages/telemetry conventions. Sean Gallagher (review): For deny/error, can we surface a counter that SRE can alert on quickly without needing to join on reason? e.g., residency_denied_total or just rely on redwood_residency_check_total{decision="deny"}? Caleb Johnson: I’d prefer the single counter with decision label; it’s standard and keeps metric surface small. I added an example PromQL snippet to the runbook for quick alerting (sum(rate(...{decision="deny"}[5m]))). Sergio Costa (review): The dashboard stub file is fine, but please make sure it won’t get auto-imported by tooling. Also add a panel description placeholder with metric names to reduce confusion later. Caleb Johnson: Good call. Added a comment at top of stub and set it to a "stub" folder not included in our import script. Included placeholder text in annotations. Nadia Rahman (review): org_tier comes from org metadata at admission. Is that always available in gateway? If not, what’s the fallback? Caleb Johnson: It’s available on authenticated requests; for unauthenticated/invalid auth, we set org_tier="unknown" and decision="error" reason="unknown" (bounded). Added tests for unknown tier fallback. Allison Grant (follow-up): Please add a short note in description about PII + not using request_id as label. Caleb Johnson: Added under Rollout considerations. Allison Grant: Approved. Sean Gallagher: Approved. Sergio Costa: Approved.
notes: Follow-ups: dashboard panels/alerts in observability-pack (Grafana import + alert rules) and fine-tuning thresholds during canary. This PR intentionally focuses on metric/trace signal definition + bounded labels to keep rollout safe.
